title: Use bsearch for lookups in sorted extended value strings.
description:
Instead of two manually coded binary search functions, let's use the C
library's bsearch function.

Also tidy up some terminology: A binary search is not the same as a binary
tree, and disambiguate VS_SEARCH by more fully describing it as a linear search
(VS_LIN_SEARCH).

----
Note that the glibc implementation of `bsearch` is an inline function.  As a result, there is essentially no detrimental impact in switching to using it... the compiler inlines everything nicely, so there's no additional function call overhead in the "calls" to the comparator function.  In fact, this change causes only trivial differences in the generated code (for Linux x86-64, at least), with an overall increase of two bytes each in `_try_val_to_str_bsearch` and `_try_val64_to_str_bsearch`.
